body: Thursday, September 10 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed sits at a knife-edge ahead of the September 16 decision. Prediction markets now price a 61% probability of a rate hike after hotter-than-expected PPI data released today. The 10Y yield has surged to 4.92% (+24 bps vs 4W), the 2Y is at 4.43% (prior close, +21 bps), and the curve has flattened to +40 bps — positive but still flat, a slope that signals the market is pricing persistent inflation and a Fed response, not recession. Mortgage rates crossed 7%. Oil at $101.39 (↑21.8% vs 4W) is the proximate inflation accelerant. Fiscal stance remains expansionary — Trump's floated $5,000 "dividend" check to every American underscores the political unwillingness to tighten the fiscal side even as monetary policy tightens.

New / Most Important: Today's PPI came in as expected but with firmer core details, tipping Fed hike odds past 60%. This is structurally significant: the US may be entering a hiking cycle even as equities sit near all-time highs (S&P at 7603, ↓1.9% vs 4W). The bond market is sending a clear signal — the 10Y at 4.92% is approaching the psychologically critical 5% level. Government bonds are losing their hedging utility against equity declines per BNN Bloomberg coverage, which means the traditional 60/40 portfolio is functionally broken again. Capital flow implications are enormous: if the Fed hikes into a $100+ oil environment, the dollar should strengthen further, draining EM liquidity. The VIX at 17.29 (↑18.2% vs 4W) is rising but still in what our snapshot labels "COMPLACENCY" — hedging demand is far too low for the macro risk cocktail on the table. The gap between equity vol complacency and bond/commodity stress is the single most dangerous setup in markets today.

Playbook ✓: Rising oil → sticky inflation → hawkish Fed repricing → higher yields → equity pressure. Textbook. Russell 2000 (↓4.9% vs 4W) underperforming Nasdaq (↓1.8%) confirms small-caps are rate-sensitive casualties.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The proposed $5,000 "dividend" to every American is a fiscal stimulus bomb that directly contradicts monetary tightening. If this gains legislative traction, it creates a structural fiscal-monetary conflict not seen since the early 1980s. The Fed would be hiking into helicopter money. This is not priced — the bond market is reacting to inflation inputs, not to the possibility of another massive demand impulse layered on top. Watch Congress: if "House and Senate" trending on X relates to this gaining bipartisan traction, the term premium in long bonds needs to reprice violently higher. The 10Y at 4.92% would look cheap.

Macro Stance: The ECB hiked rates to 2.5% today, driven by energy-fueled inflation from the Iran conflict and oil above $100. The central bank warned of "longer-lasting" inflation and signaled this may be the start of a new rate-hike cycle rather than a one-off adjustment. Bond yields hit multi-year highs across the eurozone.

New / Most Important: This is a structurally pivotal moment. The ECB had been in an easing posture through much of 2025 and early 2026 — this hike represents a full U-turn in the policy cycle. The statement explicitly cited the Iran-related energy shock as fueling inflation while simultaneously warning of weaker growth. This is a stagflationary policy response: hiking into slowing growth because the central bank has lost confidence in the inflation anchor. European bond markets are repricing aggressively, with traders now bracing for a sustained hiking cycle. The cross-border capital flow implication is that European risk assets face a double squeeze — higher rates crushing multiples while energy costs crush margins. The euro may initially strengthen on rate differentials, but if growth deteriorates sharply, the currency won't hold. This is the worst macro setup for European equities since 2022.

Playbook ✓: Energy shock → inflation overshoot → forced tightening. Classic European vulnerability to exogenous supply shocks.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The ECB hiking while acknowledging weaker growth is an explicit admission that it's choosing to fight inflation at the cost of recession. The last time this happened (2022-23), European equities massively underperformed. But the divergence this time is that the US may also hike simultaneously — there's no "dovish anchor" anywhere in the G4. Global liquidity is draining in unison, which is rare and dangerous.

Macro Stance: Policy stays accommodative while the rest of the G4 tightens. August CPI rose 0.8% and PPI 3.8% (Xinhua, [Sep 9]) as rising energy costs lifted both (Reuters, [Sep 9]), with PPI back to monthly growth (Xinhua, [Sep 9]); but consumer prices are still below target (Free Malaysia Today, [Sep 9]), and VT Markets reads stable inflation as bolstering the view of further easing (VT Markets, [Sep 9]). The PBOC again set the fix far weaker than the Reuters estimate of 6.7074 (investingLive, [Sep 9]), leaning against a yuan whose uptrend BBH calls intact (FXStreet, [Sep 9]); forex reserves rose more than expected (Reuters, [Sep 7]) and the gold buying streak reached a 22nd month (Caixin Global, [Sep 8]).

PMIs & Activity: Every August survey improved. The official manufacturing PMI rebounded to 49.8 with new orders back in expansion (BigGo Finance, [Aug 30]), still a second month of contraction (CNBC, [Aug 30]); the private manufacturing PMI rose to 51.5 (BigGo Finance, [Aug 31]) and private services to 51.4 (BigGo Finance, [Sep 2]). The external leg is booming: exports jumped 25% as the surplus widened (AP News, [Sep 7]) and the surplus topped $800bn for the year (Nikkei Asia, [Sep 8]), but imports missed estimates (CNBC, [Sep 7]) and a tech boom props up exports amid weak domestic demand (International Finance, [Sep 9]). At home, passenger car sales slumped 24% in August (Caixin Global, [Sep 9]), after July retail sales grew only 0.6% with industrial output up 4.5% (Reuters, [Aug 17]). US firms in China are more upbeat as profits recover (Reuters, [Sep 9]).

Credit Impulse: Banks are swapping loans for bonds, snapping up bonds to seek returns as the loan slump deepens (Bloomberg.com, [Sep 8]), after July new loans posted a record contraction (Reuters, [Aug 14]) even as credit growth exceeded forecasts (Bloomberg.com, [Aug 14]); reconciled, the aggregate holds up while the loan book shrinks. The 300 billion yuan of special treasury bonds for bank capital (State Council Information Office, [Sep 7]) falls far short in The Economist's view (The Economist, [Sep 8]); the tobacco monopoly is flexing financial muscle in shoring up banks (Nikkei Asia, [Sep 9]) and S&P upgraded PICC Re's outlook after the recapitalisation (InsuranceAsia News, [Sep 9]). The 3.8 trillion yuan social security fund will tap offshore bonds via Bond Connect (The Standard (HK), [Sep 9]).

Property: Beijing is narrowing developers' exits. The securities regulator rejected mandatory convertible bond registrations from developers (BigGo Finance, [Sep 9]) and China halted a key debt-to-equity restructuring tool (The Standard (HK), [Sep 9]), while court guidance aims to smooth developer bankruptcies (South China Morning Post, [Sep 9]). Goldman sees the new presale rules cutting land sales by 30% (The Business Times, [Sep 7]), Guangdong held emergency talks with developers over off-plan sales (BigGo Finance, [Sep 7]), and Beijing pledges a new development model for real estate (Global Times, [Sep 9]). July new home prices were stagnant (Reuters, [Aug 17]) and first-tier prices flat, ending a four-month rebound (South China Morning Post, [Aug 17]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The surplus is becoming geopolitical (Financial Times, [Sep 9]). The EU unveiled 'buy European' procurement rules to counter China (The Guardian, [Sep 9]) and wants initial Chinese action on the trade gap by early October (Reuters, [Sep 8]), while an Italian lobby calls for an 80% EU tariff on Chinese cars (CNBC Africa, [Sep 9]); Japan protests new Chinese measures against its chipmaking material (AP News, [Sep 8]). With Washington, China bought 1 million tons of US soybeans ahead of Xi's visit (Reuters, [Sep 9]), though Barron's warns the fragile truce could break before the summit (Barron's, [Sep 9]) and the US claims Chinese AI firms carry out 'industrial-scale' theft of trade secrets (CNN, [Sep 8]).

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng plunged below 25,000 as US Treasury yields spiked past 4.85% and oil topped $100 (BigGo Finance, [Sep 9]), closing 1.27% lower (China Daily HK, [Sep 9]); a top fund manager says Chinese stocks face Fed and oil pressures in September (South China Morning Post, [Sep 9]). An IPO frenzy has regulators warning bankers not to flood the market with 'low-quality' companies (Financial Times, [Sep 9]). Chinese banks are buying US Treasuries after wooing dollar deposits (Reuters, [Sep 6]), while Deutsche Bank says yuan use grows as supply chains reshape trade (South China Morning Post, [Sep 9]).

New / Most Important: The US-China 10-year yield gap hit a record 317 basis points, adding pressure on the yuan (bloomingbit, [Sep 9]). It is the global tightening synchronisation (Fed, ECB, BOJ, RBA all hiking or leaning hawkish) made visible in one number, and it creates a structural capital outflow risk for China. For now the PBOC is managing appreciation rather than defending against depreciation, but if it stays accommodative while everyone else hikes, the gap is where pressure on the yuan builds.

Playbook ✓: Weak domestic demand alongside export strength, with car sales down 24% and imports missing, is consistent with an accommodative PBOC.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: China is now the only major economy easing, and this policy divergence could attract carry-trade outflows and put downward pressure on Chinese assets despite stimulus efforts. The transmission runs through demand rather than rates: improving PMIs and a 25% export surge support iron ore demand expectations and the AUD at the margin, but soft imports and falling car sales cap China's pull on EM exporters, and a record surplus meets EU procurement and tariff pushback that keeps European exporters squeezed. WTI at $101.39 is a terms-of-trade tax on an importer whose domestic demand is already weak.

Macro Stance: The BOJ is expected to raise rates to 1.25% this month and reach 1.75% faster than previously expected. BOJ policymakers are publicly warning of price risks that "may trigger rapid rate hikes." Japan spent $80B in foreign reserves defending the yen, and the yen is now near seven-month highs.

New / Most Important: This is a genuine regime change in global capital flows. The BOJ moving to 1.25% and signaling 1.75% ahead means the Japanese carry trade — the single largest source of leveraged cross-border liquidity for the past decade — is being systematically unwound. The $80B FX intervention signals desperation-level commitment to yen strength. The global flow implications are massive: Japanese institutional capital (GPIF, lifers, banks) will repatriate from US Treasuries and European bonds as domestic yields rise, removing a structural bid from global fixed income at precisely the moment everyone else is also selling bonds. This is the hidden accelerant behind the US 10Y surge to 4.92%. The yen carry unwind is not a one-day event — it's a multi-quarter structural flow reversal that drains liquidity from every risk asset that was funded in yen. Watch USD/JPY: if it breaks materially lower, it signals the carry unwind is entering its acute phase.

Playbook ✓: BOJ normalization → yen strength → carry unwind → global risk-off pressure. We've seen this movie before (July 2024).  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The speed of the BOJ's hawkish pivot is far faster than any model predicted. "Faster than expected" to 1.75% combined with US pressure suggests a coordinated approach to yen strengthening that has geopolitical dimensions beyond pure monetary policy.

Macro Stance: The RBA has already hiked three times this year and multiple economists and Macquarie are now backing further rate rises in September. Deputy Governor Hunter called inflation the "top priority" and warned more needs to be done. Oil above $100 is the proximate driver — Australia imports refined products and the energy cost pass-through is rapid.

New / Most Important: The signal feed shows a hawkish chorus: RBA's Hauser explicitly warned "rates may need to rise" due to the oil spike. AUD is slipping against JPY on risk aversion. Back-to-back hikes are now consensus — this is a consumer-crushing setup given Australia's variable-rate mortgage dominance.  |  Playbook ✓: Energy shock → inflation re-acceleration → RBA forced to hike. Australian housing is the transmission mechanism.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The RBA is hiking while China (Australia's largest trade partner) is easing. This divergence means the commodity export channel won't bail out the Australian economy the way it has in past tightening cycles. The AUD faces two-way pressure: rates support it, but weak Chinese demand and risk aversion undermine it.

Macro Stance: A day after the RPP held the reference rate at 3.75% (PAP Biznes, [Sep 9]), Glapiński's press conference did the real work: rates will stay stable for a long time, possibly until mid-2027 (PAP Biznes, [Sep 10]), nothing suggests any change soon (Bankier.pl, [Sep 10]), and he hinted the NBP will not follow the ECB, which hiked again today (pb.pl, [Sep 10]); Rzeczpospolita notes this is a change from the pre-holiday stance [Sep 10]. Domestic forecasts are drifting hawkish: a hike is back in projections (Faktura.pl, [Sep 10]), Gazeta Prawna warns instalments could rise by up to 200 zł [Sep 10]. Growth revisions back that up: VeloBank raised its 2026 GDP forecast to 3.7% (WNP.PL, [Sep 10]) and Pekao lifted both inflation and GDP forecasts (Analizy.pl, [Sep 10]). GUS put the war's cumulative cost to the economy at 490.1 bn zł (Strefa Inwestorów, [Sep 9]), about €113.5bn (Yahoo Finance, [Sep 10]), with households the biggest losers (Rzeczpospolita, [Sep 10]). The NBP's gold reserves rose to 648 tons (BigGo Finance, [Sep 10]).

Markets: Thursday turned the tape: the WIG20 closed down 0.67% (Inwestycje.pl, [Sep 10]) as cheaper bonds hit the index and KGHM was routed (Bankier.pl, [Sep 10]), falling 7% while PGE gained 5.3% (Strefa Inwestorów, [Sep 10]); copper reversed from records with the White House wavering on tariffs (StockWatch.pl, [Sep 10]), and Rzeczpospolita says it increasingly smells like a downward correction [Sep 10], though the WIG20 still defends 4100 points (XYZ, [Sep 10]). The card, as of Wednesday's close, still shows the leaders fully priced: KGHM 378.0 (+9.8% 1W) going into its 7% drop; PGE 13.57 (+14.6% 1W, +22.4% 4W) and StockWatch.pl calls September a rally in PGE, Enea and Tauron [Sep 10]; EPOL 45.55 (+4.0% 1W, +2.6% 4W); PKO 118.32 (+3.6%, +7.7%), Pekao 266.3 (+3.5%, +4.2%); Orlen 159.52 (+1.0%, +2.5%) waiting for an impulse (FXMAG, [Sep 10]); Dino 35.8 (+7.2% 4W); LPP 21480 (-3.3% 4W); Allegro 45.02 (-3.0% 4W); CD Projekt 232.3 (-12.8% 4W) with a market that cannot decide (INNPoland.pl, [Sep 10]). FX is calm: Bankier.pl says nothing new came from the RPP and the zloty stayed where it was [Sep 10], USD/PLN closed at 3.7077 (-0.7% 1W, -0.7% 4W), EUR/PLN at 4.3124 (-0.3% 1W, +0.2% 4W) and FXMAG expects EUR/PLN to drift higher as the market waits on the ECB [Sep 10]; Commerzbank reads the NBP signals as dovish and a weight on PLN (FXStreet, [Sep 10]). POLGBs were the day's driver: cheaper bonds pulled equities down (Bankier.pl, [Sep 10]), while BGK still sold PLN 1.23 bln of bonds on PLN 2.13 bln of demand (TradingView, [Sep 10]) and closed a US$2.5 billion issuance (White & Case, [Sep 10]).

Fiscal & Politics: The MF reported state public debt up 7.0% q/q at end-Q2 (Strefa Inwestorów, [Sep 10]) to 53.3% of GDP (Newsmax Polska, [Sep 10]); WNP.PL says the dangerous threshold is nearer [Sep 10] after Rzeczpospolita called 55% dangerously close [Sep 9]. Glapiński added that the draft budget shows no tightening but that a 7.1% deficit has no effect on inflation (wnp.pl, [Sep 10]). The 2027 draft remains a record deficit with new taxes (Forsal.pl, [Sep 8]), the NFZ has a 12 bn hole (Rzeczpospolita, [Sep 9]). Presidential vetoes stay the political constraint (Money.pl, [Sep 9]). Tusk said Poland will block any EU initiative that raises power prices (TVN24, [Sep 10]).

Corporate & Sectors: Banks: the TSUE ruled in C-510/25 that the balance theory is allowed in CHF settlements as long as it does not harm borrowers (Prawo.pl, [Sep 10]); PKO BP says the ruling simplifies settlements (Portal Samorządowy, [Sep 10]). POLSTR is entering mortgages, so instalments may respond differently to RPP decisions (Bankier.pl, [Sep 10]) and the NBP objects to the reference rate as a mortgage base (pb.pl, [Sep 9]). Energy: Tauron posted a solid but lower profit (Rzeczpospolita, [Sep 10]); PGE's deputy CEO says ETS costs weigh too heavily on industrial power prices (wnp.pl, [Sep 10]); gas is wrecking the power market in the worst period of the year (WNP.PL, [Sep 10]), power could cost 19% more in 2027 (Interia Biznes, [Sep 10]) and a court dismissed the complaint against the nuclear plant's environmental decision (Prawo.pl, [Sep 10]). Orlen faced a black Thursday at the pumps (Dziennik.pl, [Sep 10]) and will not take over PGZ (Bankier.pl, [Sep 9]). KGHM is reshaping Sierra Gorda and adding the Victoria project (Parkiet, [Sep 10]) after the BHP letter of intent (Bankier.pl, [Sep 8]). Retail: Dino's union dispute is escalating with a strike warning (Polskie Radio 24, [Sep 10]); LPP trimmed openings to 750 from 950 but not in Poland (PropertyNews.pl, [Sep 4]). Housing: 7% more applicants for mortgages (Bankier.pl, [Sep 10]) against Fakt's reading that lending slumped to its worst in a year [Sep 10].

Geopolitics & Security: Tusk warned of future attacks after a direct threat was averted at the Poland-Ukraine border (POLITICO.eu, [Sep 10]) and Poland expects Russia to strike its border crossings (Kyiv Post, [Sep 10]); NATO aircraft deployed in Poland as jet-powered drones hit Ukraine (ABC News, [Sep 10]). MON confirmed a new Ukraine aid package with a hard condition (Bankier.pl, [Sep 10]), all 250 Abrams tanks arrive in about 24 months (19FortyFive, [Sep 10]) and KUKE launched domestic guarantees for the defence industry (Bankier.pl, [Sep 10]).

New / Most Important: Glapiński has put a date on the pause: stable rates possibly to mid-2027 while the ECB tightens, with the NBP explicitly declining to follow. That is dovish for the zloty and for borrowers, but the same day the MF printed 53.3% debt and the governor waved away a 7.1% deficit, and POLGBs sold off hard enough to drag the WIG20 red and take 7% out of KGHM.  |  Playbook ✓: CE FX weakness on oil shock is textbook; a long NBP hold with a widening ECB gap argues for banks over duration and for PGE over KGHM near term.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The ECB hiking today while the NBP talks of holding to mid-2027 should pressure the zloty against the euro, yet the card shows EUR/PLN lower on the week; the bond market, not FX, is where the policy gap is being priced.

Macro Stance: The Houthis, Yemen, and Red Sea are all trending on X, indicating the Iran-related conflict is intensifying. This is the proximate cause of oil's 21.8% surge in four weeks. OPEC production jumped 346K bpd in August but clearly hasn't offset the geopolitical risk premium.

New / Most Important: EM faces a triple squeeze: synchronized G4 tightening draining dollar liquidity, $100+ oil crushing current accounts for oil importers, and risk aversion rising (VIX at 17.29, ↑18.2%). Oil-importing EMs (India, Turkey, South Africa) are the most vulnerable. The global liquidity cycle has turned decisively hostile for EM carry trades.  |  Playbook ✓: Oil spike + strong dollar + rising US rates = EM pain. Classic.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: None today.

Narrative: The Nasdaq 100 at 29,205 (↓1.8% vs 4W) is holding up better than broader markets on mega-cap resilience; rising yields at 4.92% are a headwind for duration-heavy growth, but AI capex momentum is the fundamental offset — and Nvidia dropping on Palantir partnership news shows a "sell the news" tape.

Reported: Snowflake's AI-powered results sent its shares soaring and buoyed software stocks (Reuters, [Sep 3]). Navan beat estimates and raised its forecast, but its shares tumbled on cost concerns (Reuters, [Sep 9]). Braze beat estimates, but its next-quarter outlook spooked investors (Finimize, [Sep 9]).

EPS Upside Watch: Samsara — analysts boosted their forecasts after a strong Q2 (Benzinga, [Sep 4]), with enterprise ARR surging 50% (24/7 Wall St., [Sep 3]). Cognyte — nearly doubled Q2 EPS as software revenue jumped (Stock Titan, [Sep 9]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: MongoDB (30% revenue growth) and GitLab (40%+ net ARR growth but negative operating cash flow) posted strong top lines with cash-flow questions, and Navan was sold on costs despite a raise: the market is starting to separate AI revenue growth from AI cash flow, an early sign the growth-at-any-cost AI trade is fracturing.

Narrative: Mega-cap communications names are riding the narrow market leadership rather than any sector catalyst, and private SpaceX — rising on a data-centre overhaul and a UK defence deal — is becoming the connectivity-and-defence infrastructure story the listed carriers lack.
Reported: Everyman Media's H1 revenue rose 23.5% and it returned to profit (Yahoo Finance UK, [Sep 3]); otherwise no major platform or telecom reports this week.
EPS Upside Watch: Meta / Alphabet — digital media is set to capture 80% of global ad revenue by 2029 (NDTV Profit, [Sep 7]), a share shift that compounds ad volume for the largest platforms.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Netflix fell 4% as rate repricing pressured long-duration growth, with Disney dipping too (24/7 Wall St., [Sep 4]): with the 10Y at 4.92%, streaming trades as a duration asset rather than a defensive subscription business, so the sector's "safe" growth is exposed to the same rate shock as tech.

Narrative: Higher rates support net interest income, but the curve at +40 bps, 8 bps flatter than four weeks ago, keeps NIM support thin; mortgage rates crossing 7% will crimp origination volume even as they lift income on existing books.

Reported: Chime raised its earnings guidance as it agreed to buy Stride in a $590M cash deal, and its shares rose (Seeking Alpha, [Sep 8]). CTBC Financial's first-half net profit hit a record NT$39.5 billion, though bank NIM headwinds took centre stage (finance.biggo.com, [Sep 9]). Mortgage Advice Bureau cut its profit outlook as the housing market weakened (Mortgage Strategy, [Sep 9]).
EPS Upside Watch: Robinhood — rallied 11% on price-target hikes (24/7 Wall St., [Sep 3]), a broker levered to active markets. Marqeta — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Sep 8]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: If government bonds no longer hedge equity declines, the 60/40 and risk-parity frameworks are structurally broken, and banks would not escape that systemic tail even as higher rates help them. Success brings its own risk too: Europe's rising bank earnings spark a new push to tax them (Bloomberg.com, [Sep 9]).

Narrative: WTI at $101.39 (↑21.8% vs 4W) is a supply-shock surge tied to Houthi, Red Sea and Iran escalation; with China's August imports missing estimates and its car sales down 24%, this is geopolitical pricing, not demand-driven reflation.

Reported: Baker Hughes hiked its guidance for 2026 revenue and EBITDA to reflect the Chart Industries deal (TradingView, [Sep 9]). Sasol lifted earnings 79% as debt fell, though the dividend remains on hold (Indian Chemical News, [Sep 8]). PETRONAS saw only a marginal profit rise and lower net cash in 1HFY2026 despite elevated oil prices (The Edge Malaysia, [Sep 8]).

EPS Upside Watch: IOC, BPCL & HPCL — likely to post Rs 14,470 crore profit in Q2 (The Economic Times, [Sep 9]). Magnolia Oil & Gas — Barron's says buy it to profit from higher oil prices (Barron's, [Sep 8]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: OPEC crude production jumped 346K bpd in August while prices surged above $100, breaking the "more OPEC barrels = price relief" playbook: the geopolitical premium has overwhelmed fundamentals, so energy equities trade on a war premium that can vanish on a diplomatic breakthrough or explode on escalation — position sizing matters more than direction.

Narrative: Rate-sensitive industrials face a double headwind — borrowing costs with the 10Y at 4.92% and input-cost inflation from $100+ oil — and the Russell 2000 (↓4.9% vs 4W) captures the small and mid-cap industrial pain.

Reported: Sunbelt Rentals reported record first-quarter results and raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance (Business Wire, [Sep 9]). AeroVironment beat as drone demand lifted revenue (Seeking Alpha, [Sep 9]), with backlog at a record $1.5B (24/7 Wall St., [Sep 9]). Korn Ferry beat Q1 estimates, but its Q2 EPS guidance fell below consensus (Yahoo Finance, [Sep 9]).
EPS Upside Watch: Teledyne — raised guidance as defence, space and industrial demand accelerate (Yahoo Finance, [Sep 8]). Concrete Pumping — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Sep 9]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Sunbelt's record quarter and AeroVironment's record backlog say the earnings that matter in this sector are carried by infrastructure and defence spending that the rate cycle barely touches; the bearish call is a call on rate-sensitive cyclicals and fuel-heavy transport, not on the sector's order books.

Narrative: The consumer faces a triple squeeze — mortgage rates above 7%, gasoline tracking $100+ crude and potential further rate hikes — while existing home sales have stabilized only at depressed levels.

Reported: Chewy sank 11% as a free cash flow miss overshadowed its raised outlook (24/7 Wall St., [Sep 9]). American Eagle stuck to its annual sales forecast again and its shares slumped (Reuters, [Sep 9]). Signet surged 14% as a raised profit outlook overrode flat sales guidance (24/7 Wall St., [Sep 9]).

EPS Upside Watch: Academy Sports — lifted its earnings outlook despite pressure on consumer spending (Yahoo Finance, [Sep 9]). J.Jill — its price target was raised to $25 after a strong Q2 beat and raised outlook (Pluang, [Sep 9]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Trump's $5,000 "dividend" proposal, if enacted, would be massively stimulative for low-end discretionary — the antithesis of what the rate market is pricing. Fiscal proposals and monetary tightening pulling in opposite directions leave an untradeably wide range of consumer outcomes.
Narrative: Defensive positioning should help staples as equities sell off and yields surge, but energy-driven input costs erode margins: the sector is a relative safe haven, not an absolute one.

Reported: Casey's shares slid despite an earnings beat as inside sales growth disappointed (Yahoo Finance, [Sep 9]). UNFI beat Q4 estimates on margin gains and cost savings (Yahoo Finance, [Sep 9]), and UBS raised its target on profit strength (Investing.com, [Sep 9]). Campbell's missed Q4 estimates as inflation pressured margins (Yahoo Finance, [Sep 3]) and cut its dividend 36% (BigGo Finance, [Sep 3]).

EPS Upside Watch: Sysco — reaffirmed FY2027 guidance, launched a $500M AI efficiency program and raised mid-term targets (TradingView, [Sep 9]). Philip Morris — raised its 2026 full-year diluted EPS forecast for currency only (Business Wire, [Sep 8]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Deutsche Bank expects European consumer staples to underperform as structural pressures mount (Proactive financial news, [Sep 9]): when Campbell's cuts its payout and Casey's falls on a beat, the "safe haven" depends on cost control, not the defensive label.
Narrative: Healthcare is the defensive beneficiary of the rotation out of growth and cyclicals, and rising rates do less damage here given large pharma's cash-rich balance sheets.

Reported: The Cooper Companies beat Q3 earnings estimates (Yahoo Finance, [Sep 9]). Onward Medical's shares jumped on strong H1 growth (Investing.com, [Sep 9]). Boston Scientific said it is unlikely to meet its 2026 sales and profit forecast after a cyberattack (Reuters, [Sep 8]), and its shares slid (AskTraders.com, [Sep 8]).

EPS Upside Watch: Kiniksa Pharmaceuticals — hitting new buy points after a big revenue beat, an autoimmune growth pocket that is rate-insensitive. Royalty Pharma — TD Cowen raised its target on an unchanged growth outlook (Investing.com, [Sep 8]).
